I've been on a music kick lately, but here's what I've listened to recently.

  1. 11/22/63 - Stephen King - Amazing book. I'm a sucker for well thought out time travel stories. This is the best one I've read.
  2. Replay - Ken Grimwood - Basis for "Groundhog Day" only instead of a single day, it's a span of about 30 years. Very good book.
  3. The Count of Monte Cristo - Alexandre Dumas - A modern novel from mid 19th century France. Probably the best revenge story ever.
  4. Harry Potter - Jim Dale is a legendary reader and did an amazing job with the series.
  5. Contact - Carl Sagan - An excellent story about first contact from an alien species written by a legendary astrophysicist.
  6. The Shining & Doctor Sleep - Stephen King - Two books written about 35 years apart. Each are very good in their own way.
  7. Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy - Douglas Adams - Hilariously awesome story.

Not-so-good books:

  1. Forrest Gump - Winston Groom - It read like a really bad Curious George story. It just keeps getting more ridiculous as it goes and has none of the magic of the film.
  2. Dracula - Bram Stoker - For once, the film was much more enjoyable. It's written in a diary/correspondence format and the compliments between characters are endless. The love aspect of Dracula is also missing from the book. Very boring.
  3. Blade Runner - Phillip K. Dick - I loved the movie but found the book fairly dull.
